_README: Host-side accuracy of the task models trained for the board's fixed network (same MobileNetV2 backbone, ternary pointwise + stem convs, INT8 depthwise and head, 16-channel output). Measured with Brevitas fake quantisation on the host, NOT on the board: the models are not yet exported to the board's integer format. Append-only; set current=false on a superseded entry. sha = first 16 hex digits of SHA-256.

coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.task: object detection, 12 indoor COCO classes, CenterNet-style decoding of the 16 output channels
coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.ruler: COCO box AP@[0.5:0.95] (pycocotools COCOeval), all 5,000 val2017 images, restricted to the 12 category ids, boxes in original image coordinates; train/coco_det/src/evaluate.py
coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.lineage: pose backbone (artifacts/mbv2_pose/room_mix_w3_head32_best.pth) -> det12_tern_pose (9 epochs; schedule changed 24->14 after epoch 6, stopped after epoch 9) -> det12_tern_cont (16 epochs, images with a non-person class sampled x3) -> best epoch 14 -> BatchNorm statistics re-estimated (200 batches of 64 un-augmented train images, weights unchanged)
coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.ternary_check: 34 of 34 ternary layers in {-1,0,+1} with zeros present; mean zero fraction 0.525
coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.comparison_arms: 2 epochs on a fixed 30,000-image subset, val AP: ternary from pose backbone 0.78, ternary from ImageNet 0.39, INT8 from ImageNet 0.66, ternary from ImageNet with full backbone rate 0.56 (logs in source). Neither the starting point nor ternarisation explained the slow learning.
coco_det_det12_tern_cont_20261012.superseded_why: started from the backbone of the earlier deployed pose model room_mix_w3_head32 (superseded, not released); the delivered models start from the deployed pose model probe_tern_dc32

coco_seg_seg16_tern_pose_20261012.superseded_why: started from the backbone of the earlier deployed pose model room_mix_w3_head32 (superseded, not released); the delivered models start from the deployed pose model probe_tern_dc32

nyu_depth_depth_tern_distill_20261012.ruler: NYU Depth V2, 654 official test frames, 640x480, Eigen crop, ground truth in (0.001, 10] m, no scale alignment; train/nyu_depth/src/evaluate.py
nyu_depth_depth_tern_distill_20261012.lineage: pose backbone -> depth_tern_pose (8 epochs, NYU 47,584 frames; best epoch BatchNorm re-estimated: d1 0.748, AbsRel 0.169, RMSE 0.594) -> depth_tern_distill (6 epochs on NYU + 23,996 indoor COCO images labelled by Depth Anything V2 metric indoor Small) -> best epoch 5 -> BatchNorm re-estimated on the same mix
nyu_depth_depth_tern_distill_20261012.note: The teacher-labelled images were added because the NYU-only model gave blurred maps and placed a person at >6 m on non-NYU video (demo frames, not published).

fall_detect_urfd_20261013.task: fall alarm from video: person tracks from the detector, joints from the pose model, a rule on the processor side (host prototype, fake-quantised models; not the board)
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.ruler: UR Fall Detection Dataset (URFD) cam0 RGB, 30 fall + 40 ADL sequences, 640x480 at 30 fps, per-frame labels from urfall-cam0-falls.csv (sha 4ed29af7040098ba) and urfall-cam0-adls.csv (sha e19b2d8379538c16). Fall sequence hit = first alarm at or after (first 'falling' frame - 0.5 s); an earlier alarm counts as a false alarm. ADL sequence false alarm = any alarm. Parameters chosen on the odd-numbered sequences (15 falls, 20 ADL), reported on the even-numbered ones (15 falls, 20 ADL); 'all_70' includes the tuning half and is optimistic. Delay columns: seconds from the first 'falling' frame, and from the first 'lying' frame (negative = before the person is on the floor), medians over hits.
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.build: detector artifacts/coco_det/det12v2_tern_probe_cont_best_bn.pth sha bb42fd0be70659fb; pose artifacts/pose_fallEnhancement/pose_fallEnhancement_best.pth sha 0ec41aa0f5025452; code train/coco_det/src/video_boxes.py, train/pose_fallEnhancement/src/fall_features.py, fall_rules.py, fall_tune.py
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.source: results/raw/fall_urfd_20261013/ (one JSON per variant: grid, chosen parameters, tune/test/all summaries, per-sequence rows)
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.measured_by: cd train/coco_det && python -m src.video_boxes --ckpt ../../artifacts/coco_det/det12v2_tern_probe_cont_best_bn.pth --inputs <urfd>/*-cam0-rgb.zip --out-dir runs/urfd_boxes; cd ../pose_fallEnhancement && python -m src.fall_features --boxes ../coco_det/runs/urfd_boxes --frames data/urfd --mode track --rot --out runs/fall/track_rot; python -m src.fall_tune runs/fall/track_rot --json <out>
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.delivered: track_rot + box rule (defaults of src/fall_rules.py P)

best_box.how: best box >= 0.3 of each frame, no tracking; box rule

best_pose.how: as best_box, rule may also use torso tilt

track_box.how: up to 4 person tracks (box >= 0.1 next to a track, size change per frame within 0.5-2x, joint-following for 1.5 s without a box); box rule

track_pose.how: as track_box, rule may also use torso tilt

track_rot_box.how: as track_box, pose crops also turned +-90 degrees when the person is wide or tilted (affects the joint-following box); box rule. Delivered.

track_rot_pose.how: as track_rot_box, rule may also use torso tilt (the tuning switched tilt off: DOWN_TILT 999)

fall_detect_urfd_20261013.findings: Tracking is what matters: on the tuning half 9 -> 15 of 15 falls, overall 20 -> 26 of 30; on the test half the same 11 of 15 with ADL false alarms 1 -> 0. The torso tilt from the joints and the +-90 degree crops changed the result by at most one sequence either way. The alarm comes about 0.7 s after the fall starts, about 0.3 s before URFD marks the person as lying (test half medians). Remaining false alarms (all 70): adl-23, adl-33, adl-35, people lying down on purpose on a couch or the floor within 1 s of standing. Of the 13 ADL sequences with lying frames that raise no alarm, 6 (adl-22, 30, 36, 38, 39, 40) keep a track on 58 % or less of their lying frames (dark couch, person leaves the view): there the absence of an alarm comes from losing the person, not from the rule. Remaining misses (all 70): fall-08 is a slow fall (2.4 s bent over between the last upright frame and lying, the rule allows 1 s); fall-10 and fall-22 start with the person already bent over or falling (6 and 2 upright frames, the rule needs 10); in fall-20 the box never gets wider than 1.07 x its height (threshold 1.2).
fall_detect_urfd_20261013.note: Host prototype. The fall rule runs per frame on numbers the board already produces (person boxes from the detector, joints from the pose model); it has not been ported to C or run on the board.
